name: Preah Ream II
summary:
Preah Ream II, also known as Ram II Cau Ban Sur, was the Cambodian king who ruled from 1596 to 1597. He was an usurper.

Born into a royal family, Preah Ram II ascended to the throne after the death of his predecessor, King Ponhea Yat.

His reign was marked by power struggles and conflicts with neighboring kingdoms, including the Kingdom of Ayuttha in present-day Thailand.

Despite these challenges, Preah Ram II implemented various reforms aimed at strengthening the Cambodian monarchy and promoting Buddhist traditions.

He died in 1597, marking the end of a tumultuous period in Cambodian history that would have lasting implications for the region's politics and culture.

Preah Ram II's legacy is still felt today, with many historians viewing his reign as a pivotal moment in the development of the Khmer Empire.

"The fate of our kingdom rests on the shoulders of Preah Ram II," said an Ayutthian historian, "his decisions would shape the course of history for generations to come."
